newsitem.title: CHINA: China says book that slams West is best-seller.
newsitem.headline: China says book that slams West is best-seller.

text.p: China said on Sunday a collection of patriotic essays which is highly critical of the West has climbed to the top of the nation's best seller list.

"China Can Say No", written by a group of young journalists and scholars, reached the top of the list over the last month according to a survey of bookstores in 30 major cities, the official Xinhua news agency said.
The book contends that China has uncritically absorbed Western values and it should take its place as a world power and say "no" to America.
The book has chapters entitled "We Don't Want MFN" and "I Won't Get on a Boeing 777" in a reference to the preferential trade treatment from the United States and the U.S.-built jet passenger plane.
It also maintains Beijing should claim damages from Japan for its occupation of China in the 1930s and 1940s and that force should be used against rival Taiwan.

Some Chinese intellectuals have dismissed the book as a cynical commercial venture while others have said it has touched a sympathetic chord with many people angered over political friction with the United States and the growing influence of Western culture.

The second and third best selling books were said to be "Stories on the Return of Hong Kong" -- describing the return of the British colony to Beijing rule next year -- and "The Situation and Predictions of the Chinese Economy".
